title.narrative: Justice, Rule of Law, Human Rights, Institutions "JEDI 2"

description.narrative: The project started on 1 March 2023 and will end on 28 February 2027. The project is implemented through a three-fold approach to achieve its overall objective. Firstly, it seeks to empower Tunisian citizens to pursue their rights to access justice (Outcome I) by increasing their awareness about administrative justice, the related rights and means to access them (Output 1), and providing information to local stakeholders to support citizens in their demand of justice (Output 2). Secondly, the project fosters an enabling and more efficient environment for the administrative justice (Outcome II), equipping the Administrative Tribunal (AT) with the tools and skills to provide better access to information to citizens (Output 3), improve judicial services (Output 4), and enhance case management (Output 5). Thirdly, the project aims at enhancing human and fundamental rights (Outcome III) by making legal information on justice available to promote good governance (Output 6) and utilizing it to engage citizens in public conversations at the local and national level (Output 7). The combination of these work streams will eventually improve justice services and raise citizens’ awareness on their fundamental rights, thus contributing to strengthening the rule of law (Impact).

policy-marker.narrative: Gender equality is an fundamental aspect of DRI’s mission to promote democracy. In our view, equality is an integral part of democracy, including for all genders, religious, ethnic, and socio-economic groups, and people of different ages and abilities. DRI commits to a gender-sensitive approach and to mainstreaming gender issues in all aspects of our projects. In line with UN Resolution 132514 and SDG 5, and to ensure that DRI’s projects are designed, implemented and evaluated in a gender-sensitive manner, we have introduced a gender and diversity policy and a gender mainstreaming tool which is applied across our offices worldwide. This activity will therefore place special emphasis on gender and diversity by ensuring the equal participation of women and vulnerable groups in project activities, and, whenever relevant to the context, emphasizing gender issues.

This second phase of the project aims to continue and build on the efforts started under the JEDI I project, with the support provided by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands, to raise awareness of rights with the support of civil society organization (CSO) partners, while ensuring continuity of support to institutions guaranteeing rights and freedoms in this exceptional context.DRI use a people-centred justice approach that relies on perspectives, needs, strengths, and expectations of justice users to improve the quality of justice and reduce barriers to service delivery. It is an approach designed to fill the gaps of traditional, institution-focused programming by bridging the gap between citizens and state institutions providing services to citizens.The project will mainly target citizens, CSOs, judges and court personnel, using a dual approach combining the capacity building of partners to ultimately improve citizens' knowledge of rights and means to access justice, as well as the support to institutions of justice through organisational development to improve their effectiveness in service delivery.

description.narrative: January 2024-December 2024 The 2024 Tunisia Rule of Law Index shows a slight but troubling decline Tunisia’s overall rule of law score decreased from 0.52 in 2023 to 0.50, by -2.3% in this year’s Index. It ranks 76th out of 142 countries worldwide losing 4 places. On the other hand, The Fragile States Index (FSI) of 2024 has placed Tunisia at the 92th position (out of 179) in the context of Human Rights and Rule of Law, with a score of 7.0 This rank and score are also indicative of the country's challenges in these areas .

title.narrative: III.6 Output 6 : Legal information is available to enhance good governance

description.narrative: The project seek to make legal information available to enhance good governance. The project achieve this by producing specific and tailored publications and other knowledge products depending on the needs of the project, CSO partners and other stakeholders, as well as topics of interests depending on the upcoming reforms. These products will then be used in workshops that will engage stakeholders from different backgrounds such as government officials, magistrates, clerks, lawyers, law professors and students, media, journalists, CSO’s representatives, etc. to increase understanding, dialogue, synergies, and consensus around key legal reforms. Moreover, an online observatory to monitor case laws on fundamental rights will serve as a sustainable and indispensable one-stop destination for civil society actors, the legal community and the public seeking to continue to be updated and learn more about justice and human rights in Tunisia. This phase focus on establishing evidence-based literature on topics related to rule of law in Tunisia and building a community of practice around that can uphold their results and carry out actions to enhance knowledge about human rights and justice, and thus enhance the overall environment of fundamental rights for Tunisia citizens.

II.5 Output 5 : Case management is improved in administrative justice

description.narrative: The project will conduct an evaluation of human resources management practices and review judicial procedures in at least two administrative courts to uncover shortcomings in human-related behaviors and organizational processes that may be leading to slowing down the issuance of verdicts. This step will then inform the design of new procedures and workflows to enhance case management practices and revamp working relationships vertically between managers and subordinates as well as horizontally between staff from different departments to ensure better working processes and thus case management.

title.narrative: II.3 Output 3 : Administrative Tribunal is more open and better equipped to provide citizens with access to information

description.narrative: The project will engage the AT to make it more open and better equipped to serve citizens and provide them with information. This will be done by working with the AT to conduct open days in all administrative courts, which will bring together citizens, members of the AT, and experts to exchange information and obtain feedback. Based on the feedback and observations from the open days, the project will work with the communications department at the AT, building their capacities to better connect with and serve the citizens. The two previous activities will feed into supporting the entirety of the AT to implement digital tools that can provide services to the citizens and facilitate interactive communication with them. This phase is focused on working with the AT to become more open and capable, as well as willing to provide proper services to citizens.

II.4 Output 4 : Accessibility to and quality of judicial services is improved

description.narrative: The project will improve the accessibility and quality of judicial services, making it more attractive and welcoming for citizens to access and pursue their legal rights. This will be implemented by assessing reception services in all administrative courts to identify existing weaknesses and strengths to be remedied in order to prepare the courts to acquire the “Marhaba” label, which is a national label for the quality of reception services in Tunisia established by the National Institute for Standardization and Industrial Property (INNORPI). The results from this assessment will then be used to train the staff of two selected courts and provide them with the required equipment to become eligible for the “Marhaba” certification. After the two courts become ready to apply, INNORPI’s institutional audit will determine eligibility to acquire the certificates, and eventually maintain the certificate. This phase is more focused on enhancing the cultural and behavioral aspects within the courts and making their environment more enabling for citizens to seek justice.

title.narrative: % of user satisfaction (with people who visit the court with pre and post evaluation)

description.narrative: This indicator quantifies the improvement in satisfaction levels among individuals who visit the Regional chambers, comparing their experiences before and after the implementation of the "Marhaba" label certification. This measurement assesses the effectiveness of the certification process in enhancing the quality of court reception and services by comparing user satisfaction levels before the certification (pre-evaluation) and after the certification (post-evaluation). A higher percentage indicates a positive impact on user satisfaction resulting from the certification initiative.

III.7 Output 7 : Inclusive participation of citizens in the public debate at local and national levels

description.narrative: The project will start by conducting a rapid evaluation of human rights and local justice needs in at least two remote districts to identify human rights concerns and justice needs and grievances to guide DRI in the following activities. The information resulting from the previous activities will be then used to launch a podcast series on local justice issues and human rights topics of interest to promote and strengthen the voices of marginalized populations in human rights debates at the local and national level and raise awareness among the different stakeholders about issues of concern to the Tunisian society. This approach would also allow for direct interaction between the public and relevant stakeholders such as experts and government stakeholders and give the chance to present the information in a simple and non-technical manner. To conclude, the project will produce a radio show that will focus on selected thematic issues, which will be led by Tunisian law students who will be trained on media production to carry out their own radio shows at the local level, and who will act as ambassadors for the project after its end and ensure the sustainability of its impact.
